speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Raising children poses its own challenges, and divorced parents, just like any other parent, want the best for their children and try their best to raise their children well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The study did not attempt to determine causality, that is, it did not seek to determine if the divorce itself caused certain outcomes in children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Rather, the study examined the children’s outcomes in the following five areas and its co-occurrence with parental divorce: one, whether they obtained a university degree; two, their annual income, three, their balances in CPF MediSave and Special Accounts; four, whether they got married; and five, whether they divorced among those who got married.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: There was no clear finding suggesting a relationship between the child’s age when the parents divorced and the child’s outcomes at age 35.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF will continue to look deeper into various aspects of divorce so as to understand the factors that are associated with positive or negative child outcomes post-divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In other words, in general, children whose parents were divorced were more likely to not fare as well as those whose parents remained married based on the five factors analysed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: But it is not a deterministic cause and effect relationship.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In fact, the findings also indicated that amongst children whose parents were divorced, there were some who did as well and even better than many children whose parents remained married.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Hence, in cases of parental divorce, it is important to focus more efforts on early intervention for the children, not only to mitigate the potential negative effects but also to enhance their positive development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This intervention effort should be based on rigorous evidence from the social and behavioural sciences, and for it to work we will need good policies and the help from experts but also the support from families, communities and indeed a whole-of-society approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Today, couples who are undergoing divorce go through parenting programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Under the Women’s Charter, those who cannot agree on the divorce or its ancillary matters must attend a mandatory parenting programme before they can file for divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For those who agree on the divorce and its ancillary matters, they can go for the Parenting PACT programme after the divorce is concluded.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Muslim couples considering divorce attend the Syariah Court’s mandatory Marriage Counselling Programme, as well as parenting programmes as part of the divorce process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: All these initiatives for civil as well as Muslim divorces aim to raise parents’ awareness of their children’s needs and the importance of co-parenting in a respectful and collaborative manner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will continually review both the process and the content of these initiatives to enhance their efficacy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For couples experiencing marital stress or contemplating divorce, we have started a new online counselling pilot with the Community Psychology Hub in April 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Couples or their children can also alternatively approach any of our six Divorce Support Specialist Agencies (DSSAs) if they require counselling support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will also be introducing a new pre-divorce online portal in late 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In this regard, MSF has just completed an engagement session with more than 120 citizens, many of whom were divorcees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: They have given us valuable inputs on how we can better provide information that parents need to consider when contemplating divorce, ranging from the emotional well-being of their children to bread and butter issues that impact their children, particularly housing and financial stability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MCCY will also be conducting a similar engagement with a focus on Muslim divorce issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF provides an evidence-based programme for parents and children between six and 15 years of age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This programme is called “Children in Between” and is run by counsellors from the DSSAs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: It equips children with skills to manage their feelings and develop resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We are looking into how we can encourage more divorced parents to enrol themselves and their children for this important programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Our schools and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) provide support to all students who are facing personal challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I encourage parents who would like such support for their children to approach the network of teachers, counsellors and Education and Career Guidance counsellors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I also encourage the older students, especially those who are teenagers, to seek help from this extensive network.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: If you are facing issues arising from your parents’ divorce, you need not handle it on your own.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Please turn to this network of care and support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Earlier, I mentioned that we had engaged more than 120 citizens on the pre-divorce support portal, and that many of them were divorcees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: While they appreciated what we were trying to do, many strongly urged us to also try to save marriages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Indeed, it is as important, if not more, that we increase our upstream efforts to strengthen marriages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will also step up our efforts to encourage couples to undergo marriage preparation programmes such as the evidence-based Prevention and Relationship Education Programme (PREP) workshops run by our Social Service Agencies, which equips them with the skills to build a strong foundation for marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For Muslim couples, we provide Cinta Abadi marriage preparation programme which is now offered online to make it even more accessible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Solemnisers can also play an important role to support newlyweds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: A group of Kadis/Naib Kadis from the Registry of Muslim Marriages initiated the ground-up effort, Bersamamu or “With You”, to inspire strong and stable marriages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Bersamamu has two components namely, face-to-face (F2F) interaction with soon to-wed couples and the Kadis/Naib Kadis remain connected with the newlyweds for up to two years after their solemnisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will be engaging solemnisers from ROM and hope that we can find champions among them who would develop similar initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: They will provide basic marriage support to couples facing marital issues, especially in its early stages before matters turn for the worse.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will continue to train more MFRs to support more couples in need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We are also working with social service agencies, community and religious organisations to offer more marriage enrichment programmes so that couples can nurture and deepen their relationships through life’s ups and downs, and find fulfilment in their marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will continually review and examine the efficacy of our interventions to mitigate post-divorce issues as well as to strengthen marriages, in order to improve children’s outcomes for all families.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Divorce can be messy affairs and the children in these cases often suffer the consequences.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Just last night, I had two divorce-related conflict cases at my Meet-the-People Session (MPS).

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Our children need stability and security to grow into healthy adults and experts have said that it is important for divorced parents to remain amicable and be able to effectively co-parent, in order to mitigate what the experts term as "divorce penalty".

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This translates to about 3% of all divorces.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I take the point that, indeed, we need to intervene earlier.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I recognise the point that children may suffer the consequences of divorces if they are not handled properly and amicably.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And that is why in my earlier reply, I had gone to some extent to talk about the marriage counselling programmes that we have.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is designed to encourage divorcing couples to make improved decisions that prioritises the well-being of their children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For instance, the areas that they look at are to discuss the financial challenges they may face post-divorce, their living arrangements, child custody and access, as well as the co-parenting and parenting plan.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have various counselling sessions before the finalisation of a divorce to exactly achieve what the Member had shared with us: that we want to achieve the best available outcomes for children to mitigate the impact of divorces on them.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And what was the motivation for publishing the results of this study in a manner that, unfortunately, I think, creates the unintended further stigmatising of divorcees, achieving the effect of maybe potentially guilt-tripping them, and also the unfortunate labelling of children from divorced families.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Are there any measures within the Ministry to look into better planning such communications in future, where it can be accompanied by further and deeper insights into the factors that account for the outcomes that were shared?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I understand the spirit of data sharing and observations, but the timing of this publication and the limited scope or insights that it provided, unfortunately, created a certain effect amongst divorcees.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I was quite saddened when I saw this and I questioned myself.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Does this make it harder for couples who are already considering divorce due to very difficult circumstances in their marriage?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Because then, they would worry about these outcomes, which they already do worry about.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It does not help them in their consideration process.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We fully recognise that divorce is a difficult process and also, a deeply personal one.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is why when I started my response, I had said that it is never easy.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The intent of MSF to publish this research study is not to guilt trip anyone.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But we have data, administrative data, and we think that there are important observations that can be made from this data.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And we wanted to share it with practitioners and families, so that they understand what the data presents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MSF undertook the study to understand the potential impact of divorce.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Like I have said, we looked at divorce and its co-occurrence with the five factors that I have shared earlier.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But it is not about cause and effect.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Now that we have this information, the next step we want to look at is how we can further strengthen marriages, how we can help to prevent divorce where it is possible.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But we fully recognise that, in some instances, for certain family dynamics, divorce may jolly well be the best way out for everyone.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And if that is the case, and if there are young minor children involved, how best do we mitigate the impact of divorces on these children?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is the intent and the spirit of this study.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But I fully acknowledge and take the Member's point about the importance of communications and that is why I really appreciate the opportunity to share about MSF's motivations at this occasion today.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think the "Children in Between" programme is an important one.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But as the Minister of State has just shared, the problem really is that the take-up rate is so low.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I am just wondering whether MSF will consider making this programme mandatory, just like how we make the parenting programme mandatory as well.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I think that will contribute to certain mitigation measures and specific programmes to address those factors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is different from how we have conducted the survey as it is now, which is based on administrative data and looks at where the child is, how they have performed at specific points in time.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I had talked about the pre-divorce support portal.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, those would be the immediate next steps that we will be taking.
